newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Bellsouth upgrades NZ mobile network.
newsitem.headline: Bellsouth upgrades NZ mobile network.

text.p: BellSouth is spending NZ$60 million to upgrade its mobile phone network as customer numbers climb towards 70,000, the Dominion newspaper reported on Tuesday.
General manager engineering Arthur Neely said NZ$30 million would be spent on network coverage, with a focus on the South Island, and the rest would go on increasing switch capacity.

By the end of last year BellSouth met its target of 60,000 customers, but the company has said that issues such as number portability and Telecom Corp of New Zealand's ability to bundle services were slowing growth.
As part of the network coverage upgrade at least 12 new sites will be put in place in the South Island.
Neely said this would cost between NZ$10 and $12 million. New South Island sites include Wanaka's Treble Cone Skifield, Te Anau and Cromwell.
Other areas highlighted by the roll-out are Auckland, Waikato and parts of the lower North Island.
"We will also be able to enhance capacity and call quality in busy metropolitan areas and main transportation routes," he said.
